newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols up marginally in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols up marginally in thin trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were up marginally in extremely thin post-Christmas trade, dealer said.
Although the underlying bond market barely moved, premium levels were underpinned as offers backed off amid reluctance among market-makers to take option positions, they noted.
"It's just a function of low volume," said a trader for a bank affiliate at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatilities for February and March T-bond futures options were up 0.1-0.2 point from Tuesday's closings at around 9.1 and 9.7 percent respectively.
The market was closed Wednesday for the Christmas holiday.
Traders said trading volume today could be even lower than Tuesday's dismal pre-holiday half-day turnover. CBOT T-bond futures volume Tuesday totaled 16,197 contracts.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, implied volatilities for Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were mostly steady on thin volume.
Volatilities for March and June Eurodollar futures options stood at 8.6 and 13.5 percent, respectively.
